ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure is an NMOS transistor M1, the source is grounded, and the drain is connected to the output node VOUT; VOUT is pulled up to VDD = 3 V through the resistor RD = 20 kΩ; the gate is driven by VGS. Then reason: let the overdrive voltage x = VGS - VT. The source is grounded, so VDS = VOUT. When "just at the saturation boundary," the NMOS satisfies VDS = VGS - VT = x, therefore VOUT = x. The current through RD is ID = (3 - x) / 20 kΩ. When channel-length modulation is ignored, the saturation-boundary current can also be written as ID = (1/2) μnCox(W/L)x^2 = (1/2)(100 μA/V^2)(10)x^2 = 500 μA/V^2 · x^2. Set the two equal: (3 - x)/20000 = 500e-6 x^2, obtaining 3 - x = 10x^2, namely 10x^2 + x - 3 = 0. The positive root is x = 0.5 V. It is known that VGS = 1 V, so VT = VGS - x = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5 V.

Question: For the transistor \( M_1 \) in the circuit shown in the figure, \( \mu_n C_{ox} = 100 \, \mu A/V^2 \) and \( \left(\frac{W}{L}\right) = 10 \), where \( \mu_n \) is the mobility of electron, \( C_{ox} \) is the oxide capacitance per unit area, \( W \) is the width, and \( L \) is the length.

method.method_draft: Let x = VGS - VT be the overdrive voltage. From the image, at the edge of saturation VOUT = VDS = x because the source is grounded. The drain current through RD is ID = (3 - x)/20 kΩ. From the text, μnCox = 100 μA/V², W/L = 10, and VGS = 1 V, so ID = 0.5(100 μA/V²)(10)x² = 500 μA/V²·x². Equate resistor and MOS currents: (3 - x)/20000 = 500 μA·x², solve 10x² + x - 3 = 0 to get the positive root x = 0.5 V, then VT = VGS - x = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5 V.

method.method_draft: Set up the load-line intersection directly with VT as the unknown. From the boundary condition and VGS = 1 V, the image-grounded drain/output voltage is VOUT = VDS = 1 - VT. Hence the resistor current is ID = [3 - (1 - VT)]/20 kΩ = (2 + VT)/20 kΩ. The MOSFET current at the same boundary is ID = 0.5(100 μA/V²)(10)(1 - VT)². Equate these two expressions and solve for the physically valid root with 0 < VT < 1 V; this gives VT = 0.5 V after rounding to one decimal place.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个 NMOS 管 M1，源极接地，漏极连接到输出节点 VOUT；漏极上方通过电阻 RD = 20 kΩ 接到电源 VDD = 3 V；栅极由 VGS 驱动。推理：源极接地，所以 VDS = VOUT。题设 VGS = 1 V，并且晶体管处于饱和边界，因此边界条件为 VDS = VGS - VT = 1 - VT，所以 VOUT = 1 - VT。电阻电流等于漏极电流：ID = [3 - (1 - VT)] / 20 kΩ = (2 + VT) / 20 kΩ。忽略沟道长度调制时，饱和边界处 MOSFET 电流为 ID = 0.5 μnCox(W/L)(VGS - VT)^2 = 0.5 × 100 μA/V² × 10 × (1 - VT)^2 = 500(1 - VT)^2 μA。又 (2 + VT)/20 kΩ = 50(2 + VT) μA，因此 50(2 + VT) = 500(1 - VT)^2。化简得 2 + VT = 10(1 - 2VT + VT²)，即 10VT² - 21VT + 8 = 0。解得 VT = 0.5 V 或 1.6 V；由于需要 0 < VT < VGS = 1 V，物理有效根为 VT = 0.5 V。四舍五入到一位小数仍为 0.5 V。
